text:
elaine: Quick follow-up from the prewarm RFC — I sketched a tiny proposal for reconciling tenant prewarm signals with cost-surge detection. Want to sanity-check before I turn it into a short RFC.

devin: +1, curious how this differs from the current headroom token stuff.

elaine: TL;DR: introduce a lightweight "surge-confidence" signal (0..100) from prediction and hotpath telemetry. Use it to temporarily raise prewarm budget, but gated by a cost-surge circuit that checks short-window actual spend delta.

rik: can you show the signal flow? a drawing or tiny pseudo-proto helps.

elaine: sure — rough flow: 
1) predictive model emits surge-confidence and expected qps delta
2) admission controller receives surge-confidence with tenant id + window
3) cost-governor evaluates short-window spend delta and global budget headroom
4) if gate passes, we mint ephemeral prewarm tokens for the tenant for N minutes

sam: N minutes = ? this is the important knob.

elaine: thinking default 5m, configurable per-tenant. short enough to avoid long tail cost, long enough to absorb cold penalty.

devin: how do we avoid gaming? a tenant could craft workloads to constantly flip surge-confidence.

elaine: two mitigations: 1) exponential backoff on successive grants (grant window multiplies) 2) require a cost-surge check that compares expected vs actual tokens consumed — if actual >> predicted we progressively lower allowed surge-confidence mapping.

rik: propose also tracking a rolling decile-based occupancy metric per pool (10th/50th/90th) so we can bias grants away from pools showing tight deciles.

elaine: good idea — call it pool-pressure-deciles. we can expose it in the admission API as pressure:{p10,p50,p90}.

orchestrator-bot: note: new admission API changes will require operator migration script (admission-v2) — see #infra-migrations.

devin: what about accounting? we need to bill or debit prewarm tokens to tenants so finance is accurate.

elaine: minimal ledger: ephemeral token grants emit Events: {tenant, grant_id, tokens, start_ts, expiry_ts, reason}. Cost-governor reconciles every minute: if tokens unused at expiry, they revert; if used, they convert to billed units.

sam: edge case: a tenant gets tokens but we preempt them mid-run if global surge hits — who eats cost?

elaine: policy choices: 1) tenant-owns cost (simpler) 2) shared-bridge fund that absorbs first X% of unexpected prewarm cost then charges tenant. I'm leaning to option 2 for better UX for bursty tenants, but requires commit from finance for a small buffer.

rik: option 2 is nicer. can be time-limited and per-account cap. also makes rollback easier for rollout.

devin: how does this interact with dedicated pools vs shared-hosted? we need separate treatment for Dedicated since they bought capacity.

elaine: Dedicated: prewarm tokens map to tenant reservation units, so surge-confidence only affects allocation ordering (who gets warmed slots) not new capacity. For hosted shared pools, tokens can trigger ephemeral burst nodes if budget allows.

sam: can we get a simple config example for admission-v2 so ops can review?

elaine: pasted draft snippet: 
```
admission_v2:
  surge_window_secs: 300
  default_prewarm_minutes: 5
  token_backoff_factor: 2.0
  max_ephemeral_tokens_per_tenant: 500
  cost_surge_threshold_pct: 25   # if short-window cost delta > 25% block new grants
  pool_pressure_thresholds: {p10:0.2, p50:0.6, p90:0.9}
```

devin: looks reasonable. cost_surge_threshold_pct should probably be a sliding config per-region.

elaine: agreed, will make it regional. also will add an override flag for sales-managed tenants.

rik: rollout plan? how do we avoid a blip when admission-v1 -> v2 flips?

elaine: migration plan: shadow mode for 2 weeks where admission-v2 scores but doesn't grant. Emit reconciliation alerts when v2 would have granted but v1 did not. Then opt-in gradual gating on a small set of tenants.

orchestrator-bot: reminder: create migration issue and add observability dashboards for: grants/min, revoked_grants/min, cost_delta_pct per-region.

sam: what dashboards/alerts should SRE care about?

elaine: SRE alerts: sustained cost_delta_pct > config for 10m, % grants failing pool_pressure > 30% for 5m, and unaccounted token consumption > X.

devin: last question: prediction model accuracy requirement? we need a floor before we trust surge-confidence.

elaine: propose initial threshold: model must hit 60% recall for 1m+ surge events on historical evals across top 50 tenants. If below, keep it in advisory only.

rik: sounds pragmatic. i'm happy for you to spin this into an RFC with sections: signal contract, admission-api change, ledger/events, cost-governor policy, migration plan, SRE dashboards.

elaine: will do. will ping everyone when draft is up. thanks! :tada:
